summary: A 1932 wooden tower on Mt. Hood was replaced by the current 41-foot R-6 cab in the early 1960s and is still staffed each summer and rented out the rest of the year.

access.note: Road access in summer; from 12/1-4/30 reachable only by a 3.5-mile ski/snowshoe/snowmobile trek from Skyline Sno-Park.

visit.trail_note: Winter access requires a 3.5-mile trek from Skyline Sno-Park; no drinking water on site.

events.note: Firelookout.com and Recreation.gov both give 1962 as the year the current 41-foot R-6 tower replaced the original; NHLR gives 1964 (see resolved_conflicts).
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register August 1, 1993.

evidence.quote: The original 110 foot tower on this site was built in 1932, and was replaced with the present 41 foot flattop tower in 1964.

A 100' wooden observation tower was built in 1932, replaced by the present 41' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab in 1962. Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register, it is staffed every summer, and available on the Recreation Rental program in the winter.

evidence.supports: location, one of three towers, 1932/1962 heights, winter access, no water
evidence.quote: Originally 100 feet tall when it was built in 1932, the tower was replaced with the current 40-foot building in 1962.
Between 12/1 and 04/30, guests must park at the Sno-Park and ski, snowshoe or snowmobile to the facility
Drinking water is not available at the tower

evidence.supports: three Forest Service towers on Mt. Hood, still used to spot fires
evidence.quote: It is one of three Forest Service watchtowers on Mt. Hood and it is still used to spot fires during summertime each year.

evidence.supports: southern slope of Mt. Hood, near the Warm Springs Indian Reservation, three-to-four hour trek, Sno-Park permit
evidence.quote: Clear Lake Cabin Lookout is situated on the southern slope of Mt. Hood... The lookout tower is perched on the mountainside, near the northwest corner of the Warm Springs Indian Reservation. ... An ODOT Sno-Park permit is required to park at Skyline Sno-park and the trek takes about three to four hours.

evidence.supports: catwalk views of Clear Lake and Timothy Lake
evidence.quote: It overlooks Clear Lake and Timothy Lake in the distance.

evidence.supports: National Historic Lookout Register listing date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's description gives 1964 as the year the original tower was replaced by the present 41-foot flattop tower, but both Firelookout.com and the Forest Service's Recreation.gov listing give 1962. The story notes both years rather than picking one.

sources.title: Clear Lake Butte Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Minor source disagreement on the exact replacement year (1962 vs 1964) and original tower height (100 vs 110 ft); kept both figures in the story/events rather than resolving arbitrarily.
